message.content:
### Building a New PC – Step‑by‑Step Guide Below is a practical, beginner‑friendly walkthrough. Feel free to skip sections you already know, but keep the order for safety and efficiency. | # | Task | Key Tips | |---|------|----------| | 1 | **Plan & Budget** | • List your use case (gaming, video editing, office).
• Decide on a budget (e.g., $600–$1200).
• Make a parts list (CPU, GPU, RAM, storage, PSU, case, cooling). | | 2 | **Gather Tools & Workspace** | • Phillips screwdriver (magnetic tip).
• Anti‑static wrist strap or mat.
• Clean, flat surface. | | 3 | **Choose a Case** | • Size: ATX, Micro‑ATX, Mini‑ITX.
• Airflow: front/mid intake, rear exhaust.
• Cable management features. | | 4 | **Install the Power Supply (PSU)** | • Place PSU in the case (usually bottom‑right).
• Secure with screws.
• Route cables: keep them tidy, leave room for airflow. | | 5 | **Mount the Motherboard** | • Align standoffs with motherboard holes.
• Screw in standoffs.
• Place motherboard, secure with screws. | | 6 | **Install the CPU** | • Open the CPU socket latch.
• Align the CPU (triangle marker) with the socket.
• Gently place, close latch. | | 7 | **Apply Thermal Paste & Install CPU Cooler** | • If cooler doesn’t have pre‑applied paste, apply a pea‑size amount.
• Mount cooler according to its instructions.
• Connect fan(s) to motherboard header. | | 8 | **Insert RAM** | • Open the RAM slots’ latches.
• Align RAM sticks with slot notch.
• Press down until latches click. | | 9 | **Mount Storage (SSD/HDD)** | • For 2.5” SSDs: use mounting brackets or drive bays.
• For M.2 NVMe SSDs: insert into M.2 slot, screw in. | |10 | **Install the Graphics Card (GPU)** | • Remove the appropriate expansion slot covers from the case.
• Insert GPU into the top PCI‑e x16 slot.
• Secure with screws.
• Connect 6‑pin/8‑pin power connectors from PSU. | |11 | **Connect Front Panel & USB Headers** | • Refer to motherboard manual for pin layout.
• Connect power button, reset button, USB, audio, etc. | |12 | **Cable Management** | • Route cables behind the motherboard tray.
• Use zip ties or Velcro straps.
• Keep airflow unobstructed. | |13 | **Double‑Check All Connections** | • Ensure no loose screws or cables.
• Verify that all components are seated properly. | |14 | **Power On & BIOS Setup** | • Connect monitor, keyboard, mouse.
• Turn on PSU, then PC.
• Enter BIOS (usually `Del` or `F2`).
• Check that CPU, RAM, storage, GPU are detected.
• Set boot priority to your OS installation media. | |15 | **Install Operating System** | • Boot from USB/DVD.
• Follow OS installer prompts.
• Install drivers (chipset, GPU, Wi‑Fi). | |16 | **Update Firmware & Drivers** | • Update BIOS if needed.
• Install latest GPU drivers from NVIDIA/AMD.
• Install motherboard chipset drivers. | |17 | **Test & Benchmark** | • Run stress tests (Prime95, 3DMark, FurMark).
• Monitor temperatures (HWMonitor, MSI Afterburner).
• Ensure stability. | |18 | **Enjoy & Maintain** | • Keep dust‑free.
• Update drivers regularly.
• Monitor temperatures and performance. | --- #### Quick Checklist - **CPU** – compatible socket, cooler, thermal paste - **Motherboard** – correct form factor, BIOS updated - **RAM** – DDR4/DDR5, speed, capacity - **GPU** – power connectors, size fits case - **Storage** – SSD/HDD, M.2, SATA - **PSU** – wattage, 80+ rating, enough connectors - **Case** – airflow, cable management - **Cooling** – fans, radiator, airflow direction - **Tools** – screwdriver, anti‑static wrist strap --- #### Common Pitfalls & Fixes | Issue | Fix | |-------|-----| | **PC doesn’t power on** | Check PSU switch, cables, motherboard power connector. | | **No display** | Verify GPU seated, monitor input set correctly, check cables. | | **Overheating** | Reapply thermal paste, improve airflow, add more fans. | | **Component not recognized** | Update BIOS, reseat component, check compatibility. | --- #### Resources - **PCPartPicker** – for compatibility checks and price comparisons. - **YouTube Channels** – Linus Tech Tips, JayzTwoCents, Paul's Hardware. - **Manufacturer Manuals** – always read the motherboard, GPU, and PSU manuals. Happy building! If you hit a snag, let me know which component or step, and I’ll help troubleshoot.
message.reasoning: User asks: "How to build a new PC?" They want instructions. We can provide a step-by-step guide. No function call needed.
